paragraphs: In the Vale of Glamorgan the council's fostering service is Foster Wales Vale of Glamorgan, the new name for the council's own not-for-profit fostering team and one of the 22 Welsh council services in the Foster Wales network. It is based in Barry, and its carers look after children from Barry, Penarth and the rest of the Vale, alongside the services shown above. The service says it tries to keep children close to the schools, clubs and places they know, when that is right for them.

Every Welsh council has signed the Foster Wales National Commitment, and the Vale's carers describe what it means in practice: an assessment with a qualified social worker, then a dedicated Foster Wales worker, tailored learning and development, at least six support groups a year, at least two social events for the whole household, discount schemes and paid membership of The Fostering Network. Carers say they know both their own social worker and the social worker of the child they look after.

In May 2026, for Foster Care Fortnight, the council shared a national Foster Wales survey of 120 carers: around 80% had cared for children whose behaviour reflected past trauma, and 93% said they now felt confident responding to it. The service runs information events in Barry and Penarth and online sessions on the types of fostering, the route to approval and the support on offer.

Across Wales the minimum weekly allowance for 2026-27 runs from £208 to £260 depending on the child's age, with any fee for the carer paid on top. Our Wales page sets out the national rules, and our Cardiff and Bridgend pages cover the neighbouring areas. Ask Foster Wales Vale of Glamorgan and one or two of the services above for an information pack and compare what each offers.
